title: Partner tile copy and ops gate catalog (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a working catalog to accelerate partner tile (marketplace listing) copy, map required operational gates, and surface acceptance criteria for go/no-go. Intended for GTM, partner success, and product owners coordinating partner submissions to cloud marketplaces and publisher channels.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: creative copy blocks (tile title, short blurb, long description), required assets (logos, screenshots, security blurbs), acceptance gates (legal, security, billing), and a sample sprint timeline.
- Audience: partner marketing, partner engineering, marketplace ops, sales engineering, and legal reviewers.

How to use this doc:
- Use the copy variants when building partner tile drafts.
- Check off gates as artifacts are uploaded.
- Use the sample timeline as a scaffolding for 2–3 week partner onboarding sprints.

Quick asset inventory (minimum required for first submission):
- 1x tile title (<= 60 chars)
- 1x short blurb (<= 140 chars)
- 1x long description (300–700 chars)
- 3–5 feature bullets (clear product outcomes)
- 3 x screenshots (1024x768 recommended)
- 1x 1200x627 hero image (landscape)
- Logos: color and mono SVG + PNG, min 400px
- Pricing/SKU matrix and trial offer language
- Security/compliance statement (SaaS hosting, data residency, KMS)
- Contact info: sales alias, technical onboarding alias

Tile copy variants (pick a primary and two alternates):
1) Headline (friendly engineering tone):
- "Run LLM inference at predictable cost and latency — hosted or private."
- Short blurb: "Redwood Inference delivers high-throughput LLM serving with routing, caching and SLA-backed capacity. Start with a hosted API or move to dedicated/private deployments as you scale."

2) Headline (value-first for platform teams):
- "Standardize model serving across cloud, private, and dedicated GPUs."
- Short blurb: "Unified runtime, transparent performance metrics, and rollout controls so platform teams can ship LLM features without building inference infrastructure."

3) Headline (compliance emphasis for regulated buyers):
- "Private deployments, audited KMS, and enterprise SLAs for LLM inference."
- Short blurb: "Redwood supports VPC and on-prem deployments with audit logging, key management integrations, and optional air-gapped packaging for regulated workloads."

Long description guidance (300–700 chars):
- Start with one sentence of what we do (what problem we solve).
- Add two short bullets about deployment options and operational/observability features.
- Close with a sentence about pricing model and getting started (free credits / quickstart).

Example long description (variant):
"Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for production LLM inference — enabling low-latency, cost-effective model serving across hosted, dedicated, and private environments. Ship features quickly using our hosted API or pin predictable capacity with Dedicated; for regulated workloads choose Private (VPC/on-prem) with KMS and audit logs. Instrument rollouts, monitor token-level cost and latency, and reduce unit economics with built-in caching and batching. Try it with free credits and a deployment quickstart."

Feature bullets (3–5):
- "Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments."
- "Per-token insights, trace-level latency, and per-route dashboards for debugging and cost controls."
- "Intelligent batching, prefix caching, and automatic fallbacks to maintain availability."

CTAs (choose 1 primary, 1 secondary):
- Primary: "Start free — get developer credits"
- Secondary: "Contact sales for Dedicated/Private pricing"

Ops acceptance gate checklist (must be green before submission):
- Creative:
  - Headline approved by GTM (name: _____)
  - Short blurb copy approved and localized for EN/DE/FR (if required)
  - Long description signed off by product writer
- Technical:
  - Screenshots uploaded and verified resolution/legibility
  - Demo account for marketplace review created (username/pw note stored in secrets manager)
  - Health check endpoint and sample API key documented
- Compliance/Security:
  - Security blurb verified by security reviewer (Jasper Lowe)
  - Privacy/data residency statement attached
  - Entitlements and encryption (KMS) onboarding notes included
- Commercial/Billing:
  - SKU and trial terms recorded in pricing matrix
  - Billing contact and refund policy included
- Legal:
  - Marketplace T&Cs reviewed and redlines captured
  - Trademark usage confirmed for partner logos

Risk catalog (common blockers):
- Missing screenshots or low-quality images
- Unclear pricing/SKU leading to review rejection
- Security blurb too vague (requires SOC2/KMS specifics)
- Localization delays for non-EN marketplaces
- Legal redlines that change tile naming

Sample submission timeline (2-week sprint, condensed):
Week 1 – Day 1–3: copy drafts + creative (owner: GTM)
Week 1 – Day 4–6: asset collection + security sign-off (owner: partner-eng / security)
Week 2 – Day 1–3: technical demo + marketplace sandbox upload (owner: partner-eng)
Week 2 – Day 4–7: legal and billing review, final edits, submit (owner: GTM / legal / finance)

Owner matrix (who to ping for approvals):
- GTM copy approvals: Maya Chen (mchen@redwood.ai)
- Security: Jasper Lowe (jlowe@redwood.ai)
- Partner engineering / demo: Evan Patel (epatel@redwood.ai)
- Legal and marketplace contracts: Rina Alvarez (ralvarez@redwood.ai)

Notes, open questions and TODOs:
- TODO: build a single-sheet asset tracker template for partners (screenshot specs, image naming conventions).
- Q: Do we have a canonical trial wording that legal is happy with for AWS vs Azure? (Rina to confirm)
- TODO: add localized short blurbs for DE/FR for EMEA-targeted partners before final submission.
- Consider adding a short explainer video (30–45s) to reduce review back-and-forth on capabilities.

Appendix: copy quick cheatsheet
- Tone: technical, crisp, outcome-focused. Keep buzzwords to a minimum.
- Avoid: customer claims such as "fastest" or absolute performance numbers without validation.
- Must include in tile: deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private) and primary CTA.

Version history:
- 2024-10-03: initial draft (Maya Chen)
- 2024-10-16: added ops gates and sample timeline (Evan Patel)
- 2024-11-05: security blurbs and owner matrix updated (Jasper Lowe)
